clue.text: Don't play the old man — 'e kept giving very unwelcome advice

indicators.note: something kept is held inside, so the father figure holds the letter

blocks.note: a player who is dropped is left out of the team
old man is slang for father

explanation.surface: A father, here in dropped-aitch dialect, keeps nagging his child not to play, and his advice is thoroughly unwelcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'e is the dropped H of he, which leaves just the letter to be kept inside the father.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to drop dead is a rude dismissal, jokingly framed here as advice nobody wants.

clue.text: Bother — nearly late for lift

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
in a down clue, lifting something makes it read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at being almost too late to catch a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: TARDY loses its last letter to give TARD, which is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of annoyance, interjections used when something goes wrong.

clue.text: Blades score midway through — no way back for Arsenal

indicators.note: midway through points to the central letter of the word
back means the word for way is read in the opposite direction
no means the reversed string is removed from the team name

blocks.note: the middle of the five letters
the football club, taken as written
a lane is a way or road

explanation.surface: A football report: the Blades (Sheffield United's nickname) score halfway through, and Arsenal can't come back.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blades is Sheffield United's nickname, which makes the first word look like a team; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The blade is the flat end of an oar, so blades is rowing slang for the oars themselves.

clue.text: Picked up taps oddly found in outbuilding — they may need plumbing

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and further odd-numbered letters
found in means sitting inside the outer word
in a down clue, picking something up turns it to read from the bottom upward

explanation.surface: A plumber finds taps in a garden shed which need fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plumbing' is the trap: here it means measuring depth with a plumb line, not pipework.
explanation.definitionFit: To plumb is to sound or measure the depth of water, so deep places are what get plumbed.

clue.text: Piteous asides about being fat

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are turned around and reset in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone makes pitiful little remarks about being overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Adipose tissue is the body's fat-storing tissue, the medical name for fat.

clue.text: Repeated phrase over in American state — definitely

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word reads backwards
in places the turned word inside the abbreviation

blocks.note: a riff is a repeated musical phrase

explanation.surface: A slogan is repeated all over one American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'American state' looks like one unit, but state belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to declare or assert something firmly, i.e. to state it positively.

clue.text: It's true corporation employs old dogsbody

indicators.note: to employ is to take on, so the combined words take in the letter

blocks.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly

explanation.surface: A firm declares it really does keep an elderly gofer on the payroll.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation as a pot belly is a dated joke the clue hides behind the business sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a servant or employee who does all kinds of menial jobs, the same as a dogsbody.

clue.text: Ban tuition for developing medical procedure

indicators.note: something developing is changing form, so the letters change their order

explanation.surface: A call to stop teaching a new surgical technique.
explanation.definitionFit: Intubation, putting a tube into the windpipe, is a medical procedure, often done before surgery.

clue.text: Could be my one guarantee of getting paid

blocks.note: first meaning, cryptic: a rearrangement of the letters of 'my one' is one ordering of the word for cash
second meaning: a prepaid payment slip bought from a post office

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a slip of paper might be their assurance of payment.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, 'my one' is a reordering of MONEY, which makes it a money order in the literal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A money order is a prepaid payment document, so the payee is assured the funds exist.

clue.text: Empress with a hold on power last to get stripped

indicators.note: stripped means the outer layer is removed, so first and last letters go

blocks.note: P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: An empress clinging to power is finally to be deposed.
explanation.walkthrough: FINAL loses its outer letters to leave INA. Agrippina the Younger was a Roman empress, mother of Nero.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrippina the Younger was a Roman empress, the wife of Claudius and mother of Nero.

clue.text: Formally await release in solitary?

indicators.note: released letters are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner in solitary confinement waits officially for release.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition: a prisoner in solitary is cut off, though the phrase usually means a peaceful retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in solitary confinement is isolated from everyone and everything, a grim version of a getaway.

clue.text: Caught president losing head — failed to observe queuing etiquette

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A president is caught and beheaded; separately someone pushes into a queue.
explanation.walkthrough: The president is Russia's, the most familiar head of state with a five-letter surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut in is to push into a queue ahead of others, a breach of orderly waiting.

clue.text: Blow-by-blow account at first after cast get very angry

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word before it
to blow something is to wreck it, so the letters before it are scattered

explanation.surface: A detailed account of a fight, beginning after a punch is thrown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow-by-blow' looks like one phrase, but its last word is the signal to rearrange the first two. 'After' puts THROW in front of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a wobbly is British slang for having a tantrum or losing one's temper.

clue.text: Green investments?

blocks.note: surface reading: environmentally friendly places to put one's savings
setter's reading: money put towards planting leafy boundaries, which are literally green

explanation.walkthrough: Green suggests eco-friendly finance; the answer is speculative funds, yet read literally it is money for planting a garden boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedge funds are pooled investment vehicles; a hedge is also a green row of shrubs, hence the pun.

clue.text: After storm dawned fair everywhere

indicators.note: a storm throws things into disarray, so after it the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: After a night of storms, the morning broke bright across the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Far and wide means over a great area, in all directions, so the same as everywhere.

clue.text: Marketplace at side of garage — park here

indicators.note: side of points to an edge letter, here the closing one

blocks.note: a parking bay is where one parks

explanation.surface: Directions to a market held beside a garage, with parking on site.
explanation.definitionFit: eBay is an online marketplace where people buy and sell goods by auction.

clue.text: Ant and Dec finally speak after two pages

indicators.note: finally takes only the closing letter of the name

blocks.note: a leaf of a book has two pages, front and back

explanation.surface: Ant and Dec, a famous British TV presenting duo, take turns to speak after a couple of pages of script.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a famous British TV double act, so Ant reads as a name; it is the definition, an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A leafcutter is a kind of ant that cuts leaves to cultivate fungus in its nest.

clue.text: It used to be played for a year out of season

indicators.note: being out of the season word means wrapping around its outside

blocks.note: per means for each, as in per annum
to season food is to salt it

explanation.surface: Something, perhaps a sport, used to be played for a year outside its proper season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Played' suggests a game, but it is a musical instrument; 'for a' is the Latin-derived per of per annum.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument plucked like a zither, no longer in common use.

clue.text: Gross behind? It's fantastic! Instinct's to visit (her husband's often away)

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside, so this word enters the exclamation

blocks.note: GR is the abbreviation for gross, 144
ass is US slang for the backside
the id is the instinctive part of the psyche in Freud

explanation.surface: Someone is ogling a disgusting backside and finds it great, against their better instincts.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed definition is a description of the woman rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass widow is a woman whose husband is frequently absent, for work or sport, leaving her alone.

clue.text: Two keen to reveal like Harry and Meghan?

indicators.note: to reveal means the letters are uncovered inside the phrase in front

explanation.surface: A pair eager to tell all about the royal couple who left Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have been labelled woke by critics, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Woke is an adjective for being alert to social injustice, a label often given to the Sussexes by tabloids.

clue.text: Spoilsports! Initially one stops Charles doing what he likes

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the exclaimed word
something that stops a gap plugs it, so it sits inside the royal title

explanation.surface: A rebuke to killjoys who stop King Charles enjoying himself.
explanation.walkthrough: S, then I inside KING. King Charles has long been a keen skier, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles is a known keen skier who often holidayed at Klosters, so skiing is something he likes doing.

clue.text: Cons getting signs of approval — nonsense!

blocks.note: a tick marks something as correct

explanation.surface: An exasperated reaction to swindlers being given approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiddlesticks is an old-fashioned exclamation meaning rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: President leaving Hampstead going west — it's on the front page

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so that letter goes out of the place name
going west means being ruined, so the letters left are broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: the north London district, taken as written

explanation.surface: Front-page news: the President moves out of Hampstead, a wealthy London suburb, to head west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' looks like a direction for a reversal, but reading HAMSTEAD backwards fails; it is slang for being wrecked, so the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A masthead is the newspaper's title printed across the top of its front page.

clue.text: See 22
Simple — water's receding

indicators.note: receding means moving back, so the brand reads from end to start

blocks.note: Evian is a brand of bottled mineral water

explanation.surface: An observation that the tide going out is a simple matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means artless or unsophisticated, which is one sense of simple.

clue.text: Time to rule heartlessly — destroy!

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is taken out

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
to dictate is to rule autocratically

explanation.surface: A tyrant announces the moment for ruthless rule and annihilation.
explanation.walkthrough: DICTATE loses its middle T to give DICATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out completely, so to destroy utterly.

clue.text: Crow singing to female rather softly — recital ends

indicators.note: ends picks out the final letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A crow sings quietly to a hen, its little recital fading out.
explanation.walkthrough: Crow reads as a bird, but it is the American singer Sheryl Crow.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheryl Crow is an American singer-songwriter, so her first name completes the singing Crow.

clue.text: Badly affected blonde's retired

indicators.note: read as is, saying the fair-haired one has gone to rest, so is lying in what the next word suggests

blocks.note: someone who has retired for the night has gone to bed
blonde hair is light in colour

explanation.surface: A fair-haired person has gone to bed early, feeling poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'blonde's retired' as the blonde is tucked up for the night, which is how one word ends up inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Blighted means spoiled or harmed, as crops are by blight, so badly affected.
